jalousie2.r1_d: The behaviours you've described don't show problematic jealousy in your partner. You seem to have built a relationship based on trust. If you're here because something recently put you on alert, trust your instincts, not just the numbers.
jalousie2.r2_d: Your partner shows mild signs of jealousy, within proportions that remain within normal relational range. This level says they care about you and may sometimes have insecurities, which is human. As long as these behaviours don't create pressure or control, there's no alarm to raise.
jalousie2.r3_d: Your partner's behaviours point to a moderate but real jealousy. Certain situations create tension and you feel them monitor or question in ways that sometimes weigh on you. This is a good time to talk about it calmly, before habits set in. An open conversation about what you both feel can change a lot.
jalousie2.r4_d: What you describe points to a jealousy that is starting to affect your freedom and daily life. You may already be changing some of your behaviours to avoid conflict. That's an important signal. Jealousy at this level isn't just a matter of temperament, it needs to be addressed directly in the relationship.
jalousie2.r5_d: What you've described goes beyond ordinary jealousy. The level of monitoring, control or pressure you're experiencing deserves to be taken seriously. You don't have to normalise what you feel. If you feel constrained in your relationship, if you calculate your actions to avoid reactions, it's important to talk to someone you trust.
